partner_json_extract.hero: Uber × Navier — India's ride-hail leader, on the water
partner_json_extract.why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, ~10x more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable with no charging dependency, and autonomy-ready. A ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives next door; Kochi's electric Water Metro proves India's clean-ferry appetite; and India's busiest coastal flows - Mumbai<->Alibaug, Port Blair<->Havelock - run on slow, ageing diesel craft. The category gets claimed cluster-by-cluster.
partner_json_extract.network_thesis: One app. India's coastal and river markets. Uber's water layer. | India is a coastline of harbours, tidal rivers, backwaters and island archipelagos — and no mobility platform owns the water. The same in-app foiling tier extends to Mumbai's harbour, Goa's coast, Kerala's backwaters, the Andaman islands, Kolkata's Hooghly and Chennai's ECR coast.
partner_json_extract.multimodal_fit: Uber already runs the hard parts - real-time demand, dispatch, dynamic pricing and a vast captain-partner network across India. A foiling water tier slots straight in: same app, captain-partners on the water, the water leg booked door-to-door with the Uber auto or bike to and from the jetty.
partner_json_extract.differentiation: {'why_navier': "Software-defined and autonomy-ready; a factory in Turkey for supply; and a ~100-vessel network already proving the model in the Maldives - directly relevant to India's coastline and archipelagos. The water is the ownable surface Rapido's rivals ignore."}
